listing.title: SZ Candelilla Wax, Double Refined (Beeswax Substitute for Vegans), 8 oz. For DIY Cosmetics, Soaps, Candles or any Craft Project.
bullets: Candelilla Wax is light brown to pale yellow, plant, hard brittle, slightly tacky and lustrous wax with distinctive odor.
Used in making cosmetics such as Lipsticks, Mascaras, Decorative Cosmetics, Lip Balms, Salves, Ointments. Suitable for natural, green and vegans cosmetics formulations (recipes).

Adds lubricity, skin protective and water repellent film and slip (glide) to DIY homemade skin, lip and hair care products. It is mostly used mixed with other waxes to harden them without raising their melting point (temperature at which wax turns into formula). Just be aware that this wax does not reach its maximum hardness for several days after cooling.

To incorporate into your DIY cosmetics products: combine together with your other oils, butters (mango, kokum, cupuacu) and waxes (carnauba, jojoba, sunflower) and heat up while stirring until everything is melted and uniform. Melting temperature of this wax is 146ºF-164ºF (68º-73ºC).
Product comes in a convenient resealable stand up pouch with zip lock that is easy to store and easy to use. Wax could come in form of flakes or prills; form does not affect wax quality.
description: INCI name: Cerifera (Candelilla) Wax; EU name: Candelilla Cera. Wax is used in various industries: personal care, food, pharmaceutical and for industrial applications. It is used for making varnish and in cosmetic industry it is used as a component of balms (including lip balms), lotion bars, lipsticks, ointments. This wax is harder than Beeswax; but it is softer than Carnauba Wax; candelilla wax can be used as a substitute for both of them with some modifications.

bullets: Moisturizer – After dispensing any facial moisturizer onto your palm, try adding 5-6 drops of jojoba oil to make it into a super-moisturizer. Flakiness will subside and the moisturizer will have an improved feel on your skin.

Hair conditioner – You can mix a few drops of jojoba oil into your current conditioner or use jojoba oil on its own in the shower.* You can also add it to damp hair before drying. Also, you can add it to dry hair to promote shine. Jojoba oil also moisturizes the scalp, helping prevent dandruff.

Make-up remover – Since jojoba oil is not an eye irritant, nor allergenic, you can use it to remove eye makeup. It also easily removes foundation, blush, and lipstick. Lip balm – Apply a few drops onto your finger and apply to your lips for an extra-light alternative to lip balm. Lots of lip balms tend to contain comedogenic (clogs pores) ingredients, so jojoba oil is a nice alternative.
description: What is jojoba oil? Jojoba (pronounced ho-HO-ba) oil is a botanical extract of the seed of the jojoba tree (Simmondsia chinenis). Technically it is not actually an oil, but rather what is called a wax ester. Why do we care? Because out of all of the compounds in nature, this wax ester is the most similar to human skin oil (sebum). It is theorized that applying jojoba to the skin can "trick" the skin into thinking it is producing enough oil, thus balancing oil production. The bottom line for acne-prone people is that jojoba oil is non-comedogenic so you can use it without fear. Benefits of jojoba oil Provides all day moisturization – jojoba oil doesn't evaporate like water based moisturizers can. It is theorized, but not yet proven, that because jojoba oil is so similar to human skin oil, it can "trick" the skin into thinking it has produced enough oil and thus balance oil production. Very stable – jojoba oil does not become rancid or lose antioxidants even after long periods of storage. Spreads well and absorbs well. The organic variety is free of pesticides, GMOs, and is sustainably farmed. Massage oil – Jojoba oil is perhaps the best massage oil on earth. A little goes a long way and for people with body acne is a welcome non-comedogenic option. Note: The skin irritation which sometimes comes with massage may still promote breakouts. Shave prep - For men, put 8-10 drops or more of jojoba oil on your beard area beneath your shaving cream (lather from your cleanser or other non-comedogenic shaving cream) for a more comfortable shave. This helps prevent razor burn and leaves your skin feeling nice and soft.
